Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a classic SILAC-based AP-MS (Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry) to identify binding partners of the YL2 fragment. While the biological study focuses heavily on tyrosine phosphorylation, the mass spectrometry part described in the methods and PRIDE metadata is a global protein interaction screen using SILAC, not a phosphoproteomic enrichment (no TiO2/IMAC mentioned for the MS run).

scope: Anti-Myc immunoprecipitates from both samples were mixed together, the combined sample was digested with trypsin, and high-resolution liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS-MS) analysis was performed.

A SILAC IP experiment was performed using unlabelled HEK293T cells expressing a control L1-Myc construct, and heavy labelled cells expressing YL2-Myc. An anti-Myc IP was performed to pull down interacting proteins.
